code_label: Quantum finance as an emerging cross-discipline
text_span: Quantum finance is an upcoming cross-discipline of financial engineering with the integration of quantum field theory, classical finance theory, computer science, and artificial intelligence (AI) technology
rationale: States the paper’s broad topical framing and motivation for applying quantum methods in finance.

code_label: Finance as a major QML application area
text_span: a major focus area is aspects of finance
rationale: Identifies finance as a central application domain for quantum machine learning.

code_label: Paper extends prior work with new datasets and analysis
text_span: This work significantly extends previous works done by authors [21, 49] by adding LSTM, QLSTM for time-series, extensive GPU and CUDA-Q based training/test loss analysis and new real-life stock data for the qGAN section.
rationale: Describes the paper’s stated extension over prior work and the added experimental components.

code_label: Quantum computing may speed up financial calculations
text_span: Financial institutions are performing enormous tasks of numerical calculation in their daily works, and promise of quantum computing to speed up such tasks is enticing.
rationale: Motivates the work by claiming potential computational benefits in finance.

code_label: Monte Carlo simulation is expensive classically
text_span: This process tends to make classical Monte Carlo an expensive process, both computationally and time-wise.
rationale: Identifies a computational bottleneck that motivates quantum approaches.

code_label: Quantum computers are a natural fit for Monte Carlo
text_span: Quantum computers are deemed to be a natural fit to solve Monte Carlo simulations
rationale: States a key motivation for quantum methods in financial simulation.

code_label: Practical implementation remains limited
text_span: practical implementation of these with real life data are yet to be done.
rationale: Explicitly notes a gap between theory and real-world implementation.

code_label: Three hybrid algorithms are the paper’s focus
text_span: This paper focuses on novel implementation of the following QML algorithms as applied to financial industry: a) application of quantum-classical hybrid Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks (qGAN) b) a hybrid classical-quantum Quantum Long Short Memory (QLSTM) c) Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM)
rationale: Summarizes the main algorithmic scope of the paper.

code_label: qGAN used for uncertainty model and option pricing
text_span: In our particular case, the discriminator is a classical binary classifier. Once the data is trained by qGAN, optimization was done via QUBO (Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization) to predict the best possible crypto currency available.
rationale: Describes the qGAN workflow and downstream optimization step.

code_label: LSTM and QLSTM compared on NVIDIA stock prediction
text_span: We implement both LSTM and QLSTM to predict the stock prices of NVIDIA for 210 days till August 2024, with the same number of features.
rationale: States the comparative experimental setup for time-series forecasting.

code_label: QCBM motivated by prior work and RBM comparison
text_span: Quantum Circuit Born Machine (QCBM) motivated by [5] leveraging authors’ previous work [49], showing that Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBM) outperforms parametric models for this type of financial dataset.
rationale: Explains why QCBM is included and what prior result motivates it.

code_label: GANs can be trained unsupervised
text_span: The advantage of GANs is that they can be trained in an unsupervised way.
rationale: States a general property of GANs relevant to the paper’s modeling choice.

code_label: qGANs are a relatively new active research area in finance
text_span: qGANs are relatively very new and active research area, especially in financial domain.
rationale: Positions qGANs as an emerging method in finance.

code_label: Classical GAN instability issues
text_span: GAN implementations, however, have been found to often exhibit instability issues, vanishing gradient and mode collapse
rationale: Identifies known limitations of classical GANs.

code_label: Quantum generator is implemented as a variational form
text_span: The quantum generator is implemented by a variational form.
rationale: Specifies the generator design choice for the qGAN.

code_label: QUBO is used after qGAN training
text_span: Once the data had been trained via qGAN, pyqubo library was used to implement QUBO along with the CLARABEL solver from the cvxpy library
rationale: Describes the optimization tooling used after qGAN training.

code_label: LSTM is suitable for sequential data
text_span: LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) [36] is a type of recurrent Neural Network (RNN) applicable to a broad range of problems aiming to analyze or classify sequential data.
rationale: Defines the classical baseline model and its intended use.

code_label: QLSTM replaces classical LSTM cells with VQCs
text_span: they defined the fundamental unit of the QLSTM architecture, a QLSTM cell, as a stacked together VQC (variational quantum circuit) blocks
rationale: Describes the hybrid quantum-classical architectural modification.

code_label: Classical data must be encoded into quantum states
text_span: Classical data fed into a quantum circuit needs to be processed and encoded prior to the operation.
rationale: States a necessary preprocessing step for the quantum model.

code_label: Data can be embedded into qubits or qumodes
text_span: These subsystems can be n-qubits for discrete-variable (DV) or n-qumodes for continuous-variable (CV) quantum computing.
rationale: Specifies the encoding substrate options discussed by the authors.

code_label: QCBM samples from a quantum distribution
text_span: QCBMs are probably the most well-known example of quantum generative models promising to exhibit quantum advantage on NISQ devices.
rationale: Frames QCBM as a promising generative model for NISQ settings.

code_label: QCBM can generate samples in a single run
text_span: generation of an independent sample from a learned distribution can be done in a single run of the quantum circuit of the QCBM
rationale: Highlights an operational advantage claimed for QCBM.

code_label: Experiments ran on specific GPU and software stack
text_span: All coding and simulations for QCBM and qGAN were done on NVIDIA RTX 3070 GPU on Linux Ubuntu 22.04 LTS leveraging CUDA-Q[47].
rationale: Documents the computational environment used for the experiments.

code_label: qGAN used five cryptocurrency series
text_span: Data: Real life data were used via Binance API call for five different crypto currencies with more than 5000 samples: BNBBTC, ETHBTC, LTCBTC, NEOBTC, QTUMETH.
rationale: Specifies the real-world dataset used for qGAN training.

code_label: Extreme samples were discarded to reduce qubits
text_span: Data samples smaller than 5% percentile and bigger than 95% percentile were discarded to reduce the number of qubits required for a reasonable representation of the distribution.
rationale: Shows a data-reduction decision and its rationale, indicating a modeling constraint.

code_label: qGAN training used batches and epochs
text_span: The optimization scheme used data batches of 1,000 and was run for 2000 training epochs
rationale: Provides key training hyperparameters for the qGAN experiment.

code_label: qGAN loss functions behaved as expected
text_span: the loss functions of the discriminator and generator behaved as expected.
rationale: Reports the observed training behavior of the qGAN.

code_label: BNBBTC selected as best crypto asset
text_span: which in this case was BNBBTC, as is indicated by the histogram distributions in Fig. 6.
rationale: States the qGAN/QUBO outcome for the cryptocurrency selection task.

code_label: QLSTM test predictions closer to real data
text_span: the QLSTM test predictions, especially around the volatile peaks, as shown in Fig.7, is closer to the real life data than classical LSTM.
rationale: Reports the main comparative forecasting result.

code_label: QLSTM learns more after early epochs
text_span: Notably, the QLSTM learns more information after the first ~5 training epochs than the LSTM
rationale: Describes a training-dynamics observation favoring QLSTM.

code_label: QLSTM predicts turning points earlier
text_span: also predicts turning points in the stock market slightly earlier than the LSTM
rationale: Reports a qualitative forecasting advantage of QLSTM.

code_label: QLSTM loss shows spikes linked to volatility
text_span: the QLSTM's loss (Fig.8) shows two spikes in comparison to LSTM's and that is relevant to the noise and volatility of the nature of the real-life stock data.
rationale: Connects observed loss behavior to the characteristics of the dataset.

code_label: Training time depends on GPU model
text_span: GPU dependence: It was found that the training time per epoch for QLSTM varies significantly depending on the type of GPU used.
rationale: Reports a hardware-dependent performance observation.

code_label: CUDA-Q improved QLSTM performance
text_span: significant differences were noted in the performance of the RTX 30XX GPUs on CUDA-Q, as shown in Table III.
rationale: Indicates that CUDA-Q materially affected simulation/training speed.

code_label: Statistical significance testing was conducted
text_span: Statistical significance testing using a paired t-test on RMSE values was also conducted to assess whether differences in LSTM and QLSTM errors were statistically significant.
rationale: Describes an explicit evaluation method used to compare models.

code_label: LSTM marginally better for 50 epochs
text_span: The LSTM performs marginally better for the 50 epochs.
rationale: States a comparative result that qualifies the QLSTM advantage.

code_label: QCBM used a synthetic BAS dataset
text_span: For the dataset, a bars and stripes (BAS) dataset was synthetically generated after Benedetti et al. [27] which was composed of binary images of size 2 × 2.
rationale: Specifies the toy dataset used for QCBM evaluation.

code_label: SPSA performed best among optimizers
text_span: A comparison of the optimizers were done between Cobyla, SPSA and Nelder-Mead. SPSA was found to be the better performing.
rationale: Reports the optimizer comparison outcome for QCBM.

code_label: QCBM simulation close to real distribution
text_span: the SPSA simulation appeared to be close to the real distribution.
rationale: Summarizes the fit quality of the QCBM-generated distribution.

code_label: Further research is needed
text_span: Further work is required in this exciting area
rationale: Explicitly states a need for additional research.
